name: Virginia
summary: Statutes, Constitution and Administrative Code: law.lis.virginia.gov (Division of Legislative Automated Systems) serves one section per page at short constructible URLs (/vacode/{section}/, /constitution/article{n}/section{n}/, /admincode/title{t}/agency{a}/chapter{c}/section{s}/), backed by a public GET JSON API and per-title PDF/CSV bulk files. Justia (2025 Code, Constitution) and Cornell LII (Admin Code) are the tier-2 fallbacks. Court rules exist only as one 631-page PDF on vacourts.gov that the fetch tool cuts off in Part 1A, so it is the corpus candidate. Case law: vacourts.gov slip-opinion PDFs are constructible from the record number (Supreme Court since 1995, Court of Appeals published since 1995 and unpublished since 2002) but carry no Va./S.E.2d pagination. Subsequent history comes from the Court of Appeals' rolling 'Cases Appealed to Supreme Court' PDF, which covers published opinions only. The appellate case-information systems (eapps) refuse script access.

citation_map.notes: No law_aliases are needed: Code of Virginia URLs take the section number alone (/vacode/{section}/), because the title is part of the section number. Section numbers may contain a dotted title (8.01, 18.2, 8.9A), a dotted section (1-219.1, 8.01-227.23) and a colon suffix (18.2-67.2:1); keep the colon in URLs. Virginia's own style is 'Code § 8.01-243'. The bare 'Code §' alternative routes here only with Virginia context, because other jurisdictions also say 'Code §'. A range such as '§§ 8.01-228 through 8.01-256' is a span of sections, not one section. After 'Code §§' or 'Va. Code Ann. §§' the regex captures only the first section; a bare '§§ a through b of the Code of Virginia' is not matched, so take the first section by hand. Court rules are cited 'Rule 3:20' (Part:number, with a colon). A bare 'Rule N:NN' with a colon is distinctively Virginian, but 'Rule 12' (no colon) is not. Part Two holds the Virginia Rules of Evidence ('Va. R. Evid. 2:702'). S.E./S.E.2d is shared with GA, NC, SC and WV, so it routes here only with a '(Va.' parenthetical. Va. and Va. App. are the official reporters, with no free pagination. Supreme Court record numbers are 6 digits (YY + 4-digit sequence, e.g. 250701); Court of Appeals record numbers are NNNN-YY-D (D = 1-4, the region). Rules 5:1(f) and 5A:1(f) permit citing unpublished dispositions as informative, not binding. The usual form is 'Name v. Name, No. 0139-25-1 (Va. Ct. App. Oct. 13, 2026)' or a Va. App. LEXIS / WL cite. A WL or LEXIS number cannot be resolved to a free URL: search by party name in the vacourts.gov listings (va-opinions-*) or on Justia. There is no public-domain citation format. The CourtListener ids 'va' and 'vactapp' come from memory and are unverified. West Virginia guard: every 'Va.'-prefixed alternative has a negative lookbehind for 'W.', 'W ' and 'West ', and the bare 'Code §' alternative refuses a preceding 'Va.'/'Virginia', so 'W. Va. Code § 55-2-12', 'West Virginia Code § …' and 'W. Va. LEXIS' do not route here. West Virginia will have its own record (wv). 'Code of Va. § …' is accepted. Cross-state routing: bare 'Code § X' (also used by D.C., Idaho and others), bare 'Rule N:N' (New Jersey 'Rule 1:36-3', Massachusetts 'S.J.C. Rule 1:03' / 'Appeals Court Rule 1:28') and bare 'Record No.' / 'No. NNNN-YY-D' docket forms are separate patterns marked context_required: route them to Virginia only with Virginia context. The distinctive patterns require 'Va.', 'Virginia' or 'Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia', and a rule number followed by '-N' (New Jersey style) is refused.

sources.title: Code of Virginia (Virginia Law portal, law.lis.virginia.gov)
sources.publisher: Virginia General Assembly, Division of Legislative Automated Systems (DLAS)
sources.official_status_evidence: Section pages carry no official/unofficial or UELMA statement. A footer note says the historical citation may not list every amending chapter. No 'Electronic Legal Material' entry on /vacodepopularnames/. The printed Code (published by Matthew Bender for the Code Commission) is the usual official text.
sources.coverage: All titles of the Code of Virginia, one section per page, with a history line. A separate '2026 Updates' table of contents lists the sections that took effect July 1, 2026. Full-chapter pages: /vacodefull/title{title}/chapter{chapter}/.

access.pattern_rules: section = the full section number verbatim, including title prefix, dots and any colon suffix: 8.01-243, 18.2-67.2:1, 19.2-8, 1-219.1. The long form https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title{title}/chapter{chapter}/section{section}/ also works, and the server IGNORES the chapter segment (chapter9 served § 8.01-243 correctly), so the short form is preferred. The title index /vacode/title{title}/ DOES show section ranges for each chapter (e.g. 'Chapter 4 Limitations of Actions [§§ 8.01-228 through 8.01-256]').

automation.notes: WebFetch reads the body in full on URLs that came from a search result (/vacode/8.01-243/, /vacode/19.2-8). URLs built from the pattern (/vacode/8.01-243/ before it appeared in a search, /vacode/title18.2/chapter4/section18.2-32/) timed out waiting for permission, so treat built URLs as gated and use fetch_doc.py. Pages are ~5-9K characters of text, so there is no truncation risk.

currency.where: No currency line on section pages; the date printed above the section is the render date. The /vacodeupdates/ page states what the update covers.
currency.observed: updated sections that took effect on July 1, 2026, unless otherwise noted

hazards: the date shown on each page (e.g. 10/17/2026) is the print/render date, not a currency date
repealed sections return a page with a short 'Repealed by Acts …' notice and no former text (e.g. 18.2-62, 18.2-67.2:1)
built URLs are permission-gated for WebFetch
colon section numbers (18.2-67.2:1) must keep the colon

MULTI-VERSION SECTIONS: some pages (e.g. /vacode/55.1-1245/, ~45K chars) say 'This section has more than one version with varying effective dates', and the FIRST heading can be a FUTURE version (e.g. effective July 1, 2028), with the current one '(Effective until July 1, 2027)' after it. Choose the version whose effective-date line covers the relevant date, and quote that effective-date line with the text.

access.pattern_rules: Fixed URL; grep for the Court of Appeals Record No. (NNNN-YY-D). The Supreme Court record number appears in parentheses after the disposition. Record number → PDF is deterministic (1{record}.pdf). The scndex listing is one static HTML page that a script can parse into (record, name, date, summary, file) rows, so lookup by party name is reliable.
Static listings wpcap/wpcau (17K rows) can be parsed into a (record, name, date, summary, file) index. The script must check each PDF's caption Record No. because of wrong-document files.
